Because the GPS record does not cover the period up to the 14:26:55 cancellation (F1), the missing evidence cannot be presumed in the driver's favour; the no-show threshold in NS-1(iii) is not established and the case is undetermined on that element (my client does not concede the 3-minute wait on a bare driver statement).

The driver cancelled 5 min 40 s after the platform recorded arrival (F5, F6) while remaining stationary 39 m from the pickup (F4), and the only chat messages are the driver's arrival note at 14:22 and his 14:26 announcement that he was cancelling (F10, F11), which the rider could not have answered in time to board.

Since the driver's no-show claim does not satisfy every condition of NS-1, the $6.61 cancellation fee (F5, F8) must be refunded in full to the rider, per the rule that otherwise the waiting/cancellation fee does not apply.

This driver already has one upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days (F18), so the account-review action for repeated no-show cancellations is supported as an add-on to the refund, on profile facts only.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against me is F3/F6: the driver was within 200 m of the pickup from 14:21:15 and the platform recorded arrival at 14:21:15, giving 5 min 40 s inside 200 m before the 14:26:55 cancellation, and F4 shows he was stationary 39 m away the whole time — the judge may read the gap in F1 as mere data loss and find NS-1(iii) satisfied anyway.

events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.83)
events.body:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show dispute, so it enters the NS rules through NS-0: cancelled_by = driver and the driver claims the rider was a no-show [F5][F13][NS-0]. NS-1 requires three elements together: the "I'm Here" tap or a platform arrival confirmation, GPS placing the driver at the pickup at that moment, and a continuous wait beyond 3 minutes at the pickup until cancellation [F7][F6][F4][NS-1].

NS-1(i) and (ii) are settled by the records: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while 39 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m arrival radius, and the platform independently recorded arrival at 14:21:15 [F7][F6][NS-1]. His chat line at 14:22 ("I'm here at the pickup point, white BYD e6") is consistent with, but not the basis of, that finding [F10][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) is the element the code marks as failed: the GPS trace has a hole of 3 min 20 s between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45, so the wait up to the 14:26:55 cancellation is not covered by samples [F1][F5][NS-1]. NS-1 states expressly that where the wait period has a GPS gap the continuous wait cannot be inferred between two samples and the case goes to a person [F1][NS-1]. The records around the hole (stationary 39 m from 14:21:55 to 14:26:55, within 200 m for 4 min 40 s after the tap, cancellation 5 min 40 s after the recorded arrival) point toward a satisfied wait, but they bracket the gap rather than measure it, and a driver's written statement ("waited over 3 minutes") is a claim, not proof, and cannot fill the hole [F4][F7][F6][F13][NS-1].

Because the only outcome the trace allows is escalate and the missing record goes to an element NS-1 needs, I do not rule on the merits; I do not presume the hole in either party's favour, and the amount is left null [F1][NS-1]. On safety: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint — an arrival note and a curt "I have to cancel"; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears, so safety_concern is none [F10][F11][F13][SAFE-1].

The remaining claims collapse into the same point: the rider's "I got downstairs a minute after he cancelled" has no GPS or timeline support and is superseded by the system records, which show the driver stationary at the pickup until 14:26:55, so nothing supports that account [F4][F6][NS-1]. The rider's request for an account flag rests only on the driver's profile (1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) and on NS-2, whose flag condition (tapping "I'm Here" outside the radius) is not met here (39 m at the tap), so no flag is set [F7][F18][NS-2][RD-6]. claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while 39 m from the pickup point, so the location requirement for a no-show cancellation was met at the outset (F7).

The no-show cancellation the driver relies on (F13: "I tapped I'm Here, waited over 3 minutes, nobody came, so I cancelled as a no-show") requires a continuous stay within 200 m of the pickup from the tap until cancellation, but the GPS trace has no samples at all between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 (F1) — a gap longer than 2 minutes and longer than twice the normal sampling interval — so the "continuous wait" element cannot be proved from the records.

Because the GPS record does not cover the period up to the 14:26:55 cancellation (F1), the missing evidence cannot be presumed in the driver's favour; the no-show threshold in NS-1(iii) is not established and the case is undetermined on that element (my client does not concede the 3-minute wait on a bare driver statement).

The driver cancelled 5 min 40 s after the platform recorded arrival (F5, F6) while remaining stationary 39 m from the pickup (F4), and the only chat messages are the driver's arrival note at 14:22 and his 14:26 announcement that he was cancelling (F10, F11), which the rider could not have answered in time to board.

Since the driver's no-show claim does not satisfy every condition of NS-1, the $6.61 cancellation fee (F5, F8) must be refunded in full to the rider, per the rule that otherwise the waiting/cancellation fee does not apply.

This driver already has one upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days (F18), so the account-review action for repeated no-show cancellations is supported as an add-on to the refund, on profile facts only.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against me is F3/F6: the driver was within 200 m of the pickup from 14:21:15 and the platform recorded arrival at 14:21:15, giving 5 min 40 s inside 200 m before the 14:26:55 cancellation, and F4 shows he was stationary 39 m away the whole time — the judge may read the gap in F1 as mere data loss and find NS-1(iii) satisfied anyway.
F7 shows he stayed within 200 m for 4 min 40 s after tapping "I'm Here", which the other side will cite as effectively proving the >3-minute wait even without GPS samples.

The driver's chat message F11 ("More than 3 min already, I have to cancel") and statement F13 are consistent with the timeline in F5/F6; they are statements, not consent, but they do line up with the system records.
F1 is a gap in the trace rather than affirmative proof that he left the pickup area, so my "no continuous wait" argument rests on the absence of evidence, not on contradicting evidence.

My client's own account ("I got downstairs a minute after he cancelled") is a statement with no GPS/timeline fact backing it, so it cannot independently establish that she arrived within the 200 m radius at 14:26:55.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: his closest approach was 15 m at 14:21:50 and he was first inside 200 m at 14:21:15 (F2, F3), and he was stationary 39 m from the pickup continuously from 14:21:55 to 14:26:55 (F4).

NS-1(i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while 39 m from the pickup point, i.e. within the 200 m arrival radius (F7); his chat message at 14:22, "I'm here at the pickup point, white BYD e6" (F10), is consistent with that record.

NS-1(iii) — continuous wait at the pickup point exceeding 3 minutes after the tap — is satisfied on the system records: the driver stayed within 200 m for 4 min 40 s after the tap (F7) and was stationary at 39 m from 14:21:55 to 14:26:55, i.e. the whole period between tap (14:22:15) and cancellation (14:26:55) (F4), and the platform's own arrival record shows cancellation 5 min 40 s after arrival (F6).
The cancellation fee of $6.61 is therefore properly charged to the rider and should stand, with $4.50 accruing to the driver (F8, F5); no surge was applied (F9).

The rider's complaint that she "got downstairs a minute after he cancelled" is a statement only; the system timeline shows the driver had been at the pickup point and within 200 m for nearly six minutes before he cancelled (F6, F3), so nothing in the records supports her account (F13 is likewise only the driver's own statement, both are superseded by gps/timeline).

The driver did not abuse the waiting/cancellation facility: he cancelled only after the 3-minute threshold elapsed (F7, F11 "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel"), so no flag_account on the driver is warranted under NS-1/NS-2.

weaknesses: NS-1(iii) requires continuous waiting in the 200 m zone after the tap, but the GPS trace has no samples between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 (F1) — a 3 min 20 s gap — so the rider will argue the "continuous" element cannot be fully verified from sampling and the case should go to a human reviewer (F1, policy NS-1/G12).

The rider's own profile shows she has filed 1 dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld (F17), which is neutral at best and does not help us prove the rider's lateness beyond the timeline; conversely our driver's own profile shows 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F18) — the complainant may point to that as a pattern, though profile facts cannot decide this case.

points.response: I do not contest that the driver was stationary near the pickup (F4, F2); being near the pickup is necessary but not sufficient, because NS-1 also requires an unbroken continuous wait after the tap, and that is exactly what the records fail to show (F1).
Conceded in part: the 14:22:15 tap 39 m from the pickup (F7) satisfies NS-1(i) and (ii); my case does not rest on the tap, it rests on NS-1(iii).

This is the contested element: the GPS trace has no samples between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 (F1), so the trace does not cover the period up to the 14:26:55 cancellation and the "continuous wait" cannot be inferred from two samples straddling the gap; a driver is not entitled to the $6.61 where the record fails to verify every NS-1 condition (F5, F6).

The fee can only stand if NS-1 is fully met; because NS-1(iii) is unverified on the records (F1), the correct disposition of the $6.61 charge is refund in full to the rider rather than no_action, with the residual doubt on the continuous-wait element resolved by human review rather than against the passenger.

Agreed that my client's own sentence is a statement with no system fact behind it, so I do not rely on it; but the same rule cuts against the driver, whose F13 statement and F11 chat line ("More than 3 min already") are also bare assertions and cannot substitute for the missing GPS coverage in F1, which the system records win over.

I withdraw nothing on the account flag but do not press it as a standalone remedy: it rests only on the driver's prior upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days (F18), which is admissible as an add-on action, never as the main finding.
My own claim C2 stands only as an evidentiary point — the F1 gap defeats proof of the NS-1(iii) wait — and I do not assert the driver left the 200 m zone, since F4 and F7 show he did not.

Agreed on the fact but it is only one element: the tap at 14:22:15 was 39 m from the pickup, within the arrival radius, and the platform independently recorded arrival at 14:21:15 (F7, F6), so NS-1(i) and (ii) are both satisfied, not merely (ii).

The gap in F1 (no samples 14:23:25–14:26:45) is an absence of samples, not evidence that the driver left; F4 records him stationary at 39 m from the pickup for the whole window 14:21:55–14:26:55, which brackets the gap at both ends, and F7 records him within 200 m for 4 min 40 s after the tap — so the continuous-wait element is established by gps and timeline records rather than by his statement.

NS-1(iii) is met on the system records (F7: 4 min 40 s within 200 m after the 14:22:15 tap; F6: cancellation 5 min 40 s after the platform-recorded arrival), and F13 is not the basis of our case — it is corroboration only, so the rider's "statement alone" objection does not displace the gps/timeline evidence.

This claim supports the driver: remaining stationary 39 m away for 5 minutes and cancelling 5 min 40 s after recorded arrival is exactly the conduct NS-1 requires, and the rider's own brief concedes (F5/F6/F4) that he stayed in place the whole time.

A refund requires that one of NS-1 (i)-(iii) fail; here all three hold — tap at 14:22:15 within range (F7), platform-recorded arrival at 14:21:15 (F6), and a wait beyond 3 minutes confirmed by 4 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap plus the bracketing stationary period (F7, F4) — so the $6.61 charge stands and no refund is due (F8, F5).

The rider asks for flag_account against the driver, but NS-2 attaches that action only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while outside the pickup radius, which is not the case (F7 shows 39 m at the tap); a profile field (F18) cannot supply the finding itself, and the same rider profile shows her own no-show disputes were 0 upheld (F17).

Honest concession on this element only: our case rests on the system records, not on the driver's written statement, and we do not rely on any rider admission; the rider's "one minute after" account (her complaint statement) is likewise unsupported by any gps or timeline fact.
